sections.heading: An agriculture college at Kalavai
paragraphs: Adhiparasakthi Agricultural College is based at G. B. Nagar in Kalavai, Ranipet district. It is affiliated to Tamil Nadu Agricultural University and focuses on agriculture education, research and rural development. Its learning environment combines academic study with laboratory and farm facilities.

The four-year agriculture degree brings crop, soil and plant-health subjects into practical settings. The published course outline includes rural work experience and skill-based activities, giving applicants specific elements to discuss when comparing colleges. Ask how farm assignments and rural learning are scheduled for the intended cohort, alongside the current entry requirements and full residential or day-scholar costs.

sections.heading: Agricultural study near Hosur
paragraphs: Adhiyamaan College of Agriculture and Research was established by AERI Trust in 2016. The college describes a 122.5-acre setting at Athimugam, around 22 kilometres from Hosur. Its TNAU affiliation provides the academic framework for the undergraduate agriculture programme.

The degree brings together crop improvement, plant protection, agricultural engineering, economics and extension. ACAR also publishes departmental material that helps applicants look beyond the course title: its plant-protection section describes insect specimens, microscopy and applied insect-related learning resources. A campus visit can examine how those resources support practical classes and how laboratory study connects with crop problems.

Hostel health support: ACAR describes first-aid supplies and a vehicle for taking students requiring medical attention to a hospital in Hosur. This is a published support arrangement, not a medical-service availability guarantee. Library: A dedicated library section is provided on the official college website.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for ACAR?
faqs.answer: ACAR publishes a scholarship-support sheet covering its enrolled cohorts. It names the 7.5% quota, First Graduate, Pudhumai Penn, Tamizh Pudhalvan, SC/ST/SCC and BC/MBC/DNC categories. These are reported support routes, not a promise that every new agriculture applicant qualifies. Reported state-support and scholarship categories: The institutional sheet lists the named quota/community and state schemes and marks UMIS updates/verification. Request the current scheme notice, award amount and your category-specific documents from the scholarship office; its published nodal contact is office@acar.ac.in.

faqs.question: What training and outcome evidence is available for ACAR?
faqs.answer: ACAR provides a placements section on its official website, and the facilities directory lists a training and placement cell. A current agriculture cohort report was not verified, so no placement percentage, recruiter list or salary figure is asserted.

faqs.question: Who runs ACAR?
faqs.answer: The official website identifies AERI Trust, Adhiyamaan Educational and Research Institutions, as the organisation running the college.

faqs.question: Where is the campus?
faqs.answer: It is at Athimugam on the Shoolagiri–Berigai Road in Krishnagiri district; the college places it about 22 km from Hosur.

faqs.question: Must applicants register with TNAU?
faqs.answer: The published UG page says all candidates should register through the TNAU admission website and obtain ranking. Confirm current instructions before applying.

sections.heading: Crop and soil learning in the Erode region
paragraphs: J.K.K. Munirajah College of Agricultural Science is a TNAU-affiliated agriculture college in the Erode region. Institutional historical material dates its start to 2014, and a dated college invitation identifies its location at T.N. Palayam, Gobi.

The crop-management curriculum connects cultivation decisions with scientific analysis. Published subject areas include agronomy, soil science, microbiology, crop physiology and agricultural engineering. The course table provides concrete examples for prospective students, from practical crop production to rainfed agriculture and soil-fertility management. Applicants can use those topics to discuss their interests and request the current laboratory and fieldwork timetable.

sections.heading: Agriculture education on the Chennai–Trichy corridor

Sri Venkateswara Educational Trust, Salem, established the college in 2015. It is affiliated to TNAU, with agricultural communities surrounding its highway-corridor location.

The college describes learning through projects, fieldwork and rural agricultural experience. Applicants considering undergraduate agriculture can ask how classroom learning, field assignments and rural activities are balanced, and confirm which practical modules are available for their cohort.

faqs.question: Where is JSACAT located?
faqs.answer: Ma. Podaiyur, Avatti, Tholudur, Cuddalore District, Tamil Nadu 606108

faqs.question: Which agriculture or allied programmes are covered at JSACAT?
faqs.answer: This profile covers B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture. The [courses and fees table](/university/jsa-college-of-agriculture-and-technology/course-fee) separates the qualifications and published fee periods.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at JSACAT?
faqs.answer: College page lists Physics/Chemistry with Biology and Mathematics; or Biology with Biochemistry/Biotechnology/Microbiology/Home Science/Computer Science; or Botany and Zoology. Its displayed four-subject thresholds are OC 55%, BC/BCC/BCM 50%, MBC/DNC 45%, and a qualifying-subject pass for SC/ST. Confirm these undated college-page criteria against the intended TNAU intake-year prospectus.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at JSACAT?
faqs.answer: 4 years / 8 semesters. The college lists B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture and describes a syllabus spanning agronomy, plant pathology, entomology, agricultural economics and extension. Current detailed entry rules need the college and TNAU prospectus.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at JSACAT?
faqs.answer: A verified numerical fee is not available. A dated official fee schedule with tuition, compulsory charges and residential costs was not verified.

faqs.question: How does admission to JSACAT work?
faqs.answer: JSACAT publishes an academic-stream subject table and category thresholds on its eligibility page. Its banner asks students to register with TNAU and the college. Confirm the current university rules, because the banner year does not prove the eligibility table was revised. These steps describe the TNAU counselling channel. Any separate college-management route must be checked independently. Register with TNAU: Submit a single online application. Set course preferences: Order eligible college and course combinations. Follow counselling: General-quota counselling runs online; special-reservation sessions may be offline.

faqs.question: What is the recorded ICAR scope for JSACAT?
faqs.answer: JSA College of Agriculture and Technology: • B.Sc. (Hons) Agriculture (Intake- 175), recorded term 2024-06-20 to 2029-06-19. This entry applies to the named unit and programme.

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at JSACAT?
faqs.answer: The official site identifies RAWE and experiential learning among its teaching methods. The parent group describes agricultural specialist seminars and village engagement. The published course structure uses an English-medium semester course-credit system.

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for JSACAT?
faqs.answer: JSACAT describes experiential learning and RAWE, while the parent group reports village-based agricultural activities. A separate official laboratory page describes computer access and a language laboratory for listening, speaking, reading and writing practice. Accommodation availability, meal charges and transport arrangements for your entry year still need direct confirmation.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for JSACAT?
faqs.answer: A current agriculture-specific scholarship schedule for JSACAT was not verified. Request the scheme name, funding authority, category rules, renewal conditions and net payable amount in writing before relying on a concession.

faqs.question: What training and outcome evidence is available for JSACAT?
faqs.answer: JSA’s outcomes page gives named B.Sc. Agriculture alumni examples across employment, enterprise and higher study. It lists roles connected with Central Bank of India, the Indian Postal Department, IFFCO/MC Crop Science and agricultural producer organisations. The list is undated and does not establish an annual placement percentage or salary.

faqs.question: Who established the college?
faqs.answer: The parent-group page says Sri Venkateswara Educational Trust, Salem, established it in 2015.

faqs.question: Does the website list courses beyond agriculture?
faqs.answer: Yes, it advertises horticulture and selected agriculture postgraduate programmes. This draft’s confirmed ICAR scope remains the B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture row in the audit.

faqs.question: What rural learning does JSACAT describe?
faqs.answer: The official material lists RAWE, fieldwork, experiential learning and village interaction.

sections.heading: Agriculture study with a Namakkal field setting
paragraphs: PGP College of Agricultural Sciences was established in 2013 and is affiliated to Tamil Nadu Agricultural University. Its dedicated college website describes a campus near the Kolli Hills and additional field training at the group’s main campus in Paramathi.

The agriculture degree is taught over eight semesters and combines crop science with agricultural economics and practical subjects. Its published curriculum gives examples of seed treatment, sowing, nursery techniques and crop diagnosis. Applicants can explore how those practical elements develop through the programme while comparing the university counselling and management admission channels described by the college.

sections.heading: Practical subjects across the agriculture curriculum
paragraphs: The programme outline gives concrete examples of practical teaching: seed and sowing exercises, horticultural propagation, surveying and irrigation work. These are published curriculum components, not confirmation that every listed visit occurs for every cohort.

Explore [infrastructure](/university/pgp-college-of-agricultural-sciences/infrastructure), [campus life](/university/pgp-college-of-agricultural-sciences/campus-life) and the [photo gallery](/university/pgp-college-of-agricultural-sciences/gallery).

subsections.heading: Agricultural field setting
paragraphs: The college describes farmland around its Namakkal campus and additional training land at Paramathi.

subsections.heading: Separate student hostels
paragraphs: PGPCAS describes separate accommodation for male and female students, with ventilated rooms and regular maintenance. A current room-allocation and residential fee statement is still needed.

sections.heading: Scholarships and financial support
paragraphs: The home page describes scholarships and awards and gives a group-wide annual award statement. It does not provide dated agriculture-specific award terms; no amount is represented here as an individual entitlement.
[Read the scholarship conditions and applicability](/university/pgp-college-of-agricultural-sciences/scholarship).

sections.heading: Career support and outcomes
paragraphs: The official programme page lists possible agricultural, research and rural-development careers. The home page links a placement cell, but neither fact establishes a measured agriculture employment rate. Request a recent cohort report before comparing outcomes.

sections.heading: Agricultural education in southern Tamil Nadu
paragraphs: The Indian Agriculture College is located on the Kavalkinaru–Radhapuram Road in Tirunelveli district. Established in 2016 under Joshua Educational and Charitable Trust, it focuses on agricultural education and the farming needs of southern Tamil Nadu.

Its four-year degree is organised over eight semesters. The course page covers agricultural science alongside surveying, soils, water management and allied subjects. The college also publishes campus material grouped around laboratories, agricultural fields, farms and industrial visits. Applicants can use those resources to identify which practical areas interest them and request the current timetable for field and laboratory learning.

sections.heading: A Vellore district college focused on agriculture
paragraphs: Palar Agricultural College was established in 2017 under RS Educational and Charitable Trust. It is located at Kothamarikuppam Village, Mailpatti Post, in Vellore district and offers a four-year B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture under TNAU affiliation.

Its academic divisions cover crop science and associated subjects, with agricultural teaching units and student-support cells listed across the campus website. The extension department describes rural learning and farmer engagement through RAWE. Applicants can ask how the teaching units and village activities fit together across the degree, while confirming admission ranking requirements and the complete cost of attendance.

paragraphs: PAC instructs candidates to register with TNAU and obtain ranking for counselling as well as management admission. Its fee section refers to the Government of Tamil Nadu’s prescribed structure without publishing a verified numeric schedule.

sections.heading: ICAR accreditation: programme, unit and validity
paragraphs: The audited ICAR List II records Palar Agricultural College, Vellore and the programme labels below from 2026-03-16 through 2031-03-15. This is the scope verified on 30 October 2026; it does not extend automatically to other qualifications or guarantee renewal.

paragraphs: Useful reading: [RAWE and experiential learning in B.Sc. Agriculture](/articles/rawe-and-experiential-learning).

The extension department describes RAWE and village work, including participatory rural-appraisal exercises in Pallalakuppam.

sections.heading: Agricultural teaching units listed by PAC
paragraphs: PAC’s official site lists agricultural teaching units, while its extension department describes rural engagement through RAWE and village appraisal. Confirm the current cohort’s fieldwork schedule and teaching-unit access.

Explore [infrastructure](/university/palar-agricultural-college/infrastructure), [campus life](/university/palar-agricultural-college/campus-life) and the [photo gallery](/university/palar-agricultural-college/gallery).

subsections.heading: Agricultural teaching units
paragraphs: The official site lists an apiary, mushroom cultivation and vermicompost units.

subsections.heading: Central library
paragraphs: A dedicated central-library section is listed on the college website.

subsections.heading: Student hostels and welfare spaces
paragraphs: PAC publishes separate accommodation for male and female students. Its listed common facilities include a computer-equipped reading room, sick bay, guest room and television hall; hostel records cover entry/exit, complaints and medical matters.

sections.heading: Scholarships and financial support
paragraphs: Palar has a Scholarship Cell that helps students identify schemes, understand eligibility and prepare application documentation. The page does not publish an institution-specific award amount or a current scheme decision; ask for the exact authority notice before budgeting a concession.
[Read the scholarship conditions and applicability](/university/palar-agricultural-college/scholarship).

sections.heading: Career support and outcomes
paragraphs: The college lists a Career Guidance and Placements Cell and publishes civil-services awareness material. Individual postgraduate admission achievements and awareness activities should not be counted as a programme-wide employment rate. No dated agriculture placement statistics were verified.
[Explore training and placement evidence](/university/palar-agricultural-college/training-and-placements).

sections.heading: Agriculture and rural development at Valikandapuram
paragraphs: Thanthai Roever Institute of Agriculture and Rural Development belongs to the Roever educational group and is run by St. John Sangam Trust. Its history records agriculture diploma teaching from 1994 and horticulture diploma teaching from 2001, with degree education developed later.

At Valikandapuram, the college describes 51.97 hectares, or 128.4 acres, used for practical learning and a crop cafeteria. Students considering the agriculture degree can ask how crop observations and field assignments connect with laboratory teaching. TRIARD also publishes scholarship-cell support and named graduate destinations, which applicants can discuss alongside a current prospectus and a recent cohort report.

faqs.question: Where is TRIARD located?
faqs.answer: Valikandapuram, Perambalur 621115, Tamil Nadu

faqs.question: Which agriculture or allied programmes are covered at TRIARD?
faqs.answer: This profile covers B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture. The [courses and fees table](/university/thanthai-roever-institute-of-agriculture-and-rural-development/course-fee) separates the qualifications and published fee periods.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at TRIARD?
faqs.answer: Historical official admission page: 10+2 with the listed science combinations, including Physics, Chemistry and Biology or Botany/Zoology. Current subject equivalence and minimum marks must be checked in the entry-year TNAU prospectus.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at TRIARD?
faqs.answer: 4 years. The official admission page describes a four-year B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture. Its published subject combinations centre on Physics, Chemistry and biological sciences, but the page includes a 2025–26 form and older portal guidance.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at TRIARD?
faqs.answer: A verified numerical fee is not available. A dated official fee schedule with tuition, compulsory charges and residential costs was not verified.

faqs.question: How does admission to TRIARD work?
faqs.answer: TRIARD’s published procedure directs both counselling and management applicants to TNAU registration. Because the page combines older instructions with a 2025–26 form, its stated application charges and links are not adopted as current. These steps describe the TNAU counselling channel. Any separate college-management route must be checked independently. Register with TNAU: Submit a single online application. Set course preferences: Order eligible college and course combinations. Follow counselling: General-quota counselling runs online; special-reservation sessions may be offline.

faqs.question: What is the recorded ICAR scope for TRIARD?
faqs.answer: Thanthai Roever Institute of Agriculture and Rural Development: B. Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture programme (Intake- 120), recorded term 2026-03-16 to 2031-03-15. This entry applies to the named unit and programme.

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at TRIARD?
faqs.answer: The college identifies practical training land and a crop cafeteria as part of agricultural learning.

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for TRIARD?
faqs.answer: Library: A college library is described on the official facilities page.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for TRIARD?
faqs.answer: TRIARD’s Scholarship Cell describes help with government applications, verification and renewals. The official page lists post-matric and community schemes, but does not establish an individual award amount or current eligibility for every agriculture student. Post-matric and community scholarship application support: The cell lists post-matric, BC/MBC/DNC, SC/ST and other schemes. Eligibility and availability depend on the current funding authority rules; amounts were not verified.

faqs.question: What training and outcome evidence is available for TRIARD?
faqs.answer: TRIARD’s 2025–26 outcomes table names graduates and their roles in banks, public agencies and agricultural businesses. Examples include agricultural/rural-development roles at Indian Bank and Punjab National Bank and research work at CARDS, TNAU. It is a list of reported outcomes, not a cohort-wide placement percentage or salary report.

faqs.question: Is TRIARD an independent university?
faqs.answer: No. The audited entry identifies a private college affiliated to TNAU.

faqs.question: What does the 1994 establishment date refer to?
faqs.answer: The college’s history dates the start of agriculture diploma courses to 1994. Degree education developed later.

faqs.question: What practical land is described?
faqs.answer: The official about page describes 51.97 hectares, or 128.4 acres, and a crop cafeteria for observing varieties.

sections.heading: Agriculture within an autonomous Varanasi college
paragraphs: Udai Pratap College is an autonomous institution in Varanasi affiliated to Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith. Its 2026–27 prospectus lists B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture alongside the wider college’s science, commerce and humanities courses. Agriculture is therefore part of a broader college academic setting.

The agriculture-farm section covers crop production and allied activities, including dairy, poultry, fishery and beekeeping. The prospectus also lists postgraduate subjects in agricultural economics, animal husbandry and dairy, soil science and horticulture. Applicants can compare the undergraduate practical experience and later subject options while checking the college’s entrance-examination conditions for their intended entry year.

sections.heading: Agriculture study near Markapur
paragraphs: N.S. Agricultural College was established by Sri NS Educational Society in 2016. Located at Gobburu, eight kilometres from Markapur according to the college, it is affiliated to Acharya N. G. Ranga Agricultural University.

Its teaching farm is spread across the main campus and Thokapalli, with instructional units spanning crops, horticulture and crop protection. The four-year degree describes final-year rural experience, experiential learning and an agriculture-related internship. That practical structure is useful for students comparing field exposure: request the current unit allocations, village-work schedule and internship supervision arrangements alongside the entry-year admission notice.

sections.heading: Agricultural education in Anantapuramu
paragraphs: Sri Krishnadevaraya College of Agricultural Sciences identifies itself as a self-financed, unaided private coeducational institution. Founded in 2016 under Sri Balaji Educational Society, it is affiliated to Acharya N. G. Ranga Agricultural University. Its public contact address is on Alamuru Road in Anantapuramu.

The college’s stated academic focus connects agriculture study with the needs of farming communities, including pest management, organic production and seed technology. Its about page describes a 110-acre setting. Applicants comparing it with other Andhra colleges should ask for a current farm-use schedule, laboratory inventory and university admission notice so that the practical experience and full costs can be assessed alongside the degree title.

sections.heading: Planning an application to SKCAS
paragraphs: The college homepage carries a 2026–27 management-seat banner, while a retrievable university web-options notice relates to 2022–23. Neither establishes today’s vacancy position or current entry thresholds. Use the current ANGRAU notification and confirm availability directly. For Sri Krishnadevaraya College of Agricultural Sciences, the applicable ANGRAU counselling route now has a revised 30 October 2026 notice: registered candidates follow the stated November rank/category session and check the university’s live seat position. Being called does not guarantee admission.
[Read the complete admission process](/university/sri-krishnadevaraya-college-of-agricultural-sciences/admission-process) for programme-wise requirements, documents and source-dated notices.

sections.heading: A published agricultural campus setting
paragraphs: SKCAS’s departmental descriptions identify a horticultural garden with propagation structures and model orchards, and a soil-science teaching laboratory. Entomology material links final-year rural experience to crop-pest problems.

Explore [infrastructure](/university/sri-krishnadevaraya-college-of-agricultural-sciences/infrastructure), [campus life](/university/sri-krishnadevaraya-college-of-agricultural-sciences/campus-life) and the [photo gallery](/university/sri-krishnadevaraya-college-of-agricultural-sciences/gallery).

subsections.heading: Separate hostel buildings
paragraphs: SKCAS describes separate boys’ and girls’ buildings, each with 40 rooms. The published layout includes dining/kitchen areas, warden/caretaker offices and visitors’ space; rooms are described as shared by three or four students with basic study furniture.

sections.heading: Veterinary learning with clinical exposure at Mahal
paragraphs: Khalsa College of Veterinary and Animal Sciences was established by Khalsa College Charitable Society. The college dates its formation to 2009 and GADVASU affiliation to 2010. It focuses on veterinary health, animal production and management, making it a distinct option from an undergraduate crop-science college.

Its Veterinary Clinical Complex is at village Mahal on Ram Tirath Road, separate from the main campus. The department describes services for small and large animals, diagnostic imaging, surgery and clinical laboratory work. For applicants, that clinical setting is central to evaluating the programme: ask how clinical rotations, case exposure and internship supervision are organised for the intended cohort.

faqs.question: Where is KCVAS located?

faqs.question: Which agriculture or allied programmes are covered at KCVAS?
faqs.answer: This profile covers B.V.Sc. & A.H.. The [courses and fees table](/university/khalsa-college-of-veterinary-and-animal-sciences/course-fee) separates the qualifications and published fee periods.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.V.Sc. & A.H. at KCVAS?
faqs.answer: GADVASU’s NEET-UG-2026 rules require 10+2 or equivalent with Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English and 50% aggregate excluding optional subjects (47.5% for SC/ST, BC and DP categories), plus the relevant NEET cutoff. Category, domicile and quota conditions also apply.

faqs.question: How long is B.V.Sc. & A.H. at KCVAS?
faqs.answer: 5½ years. B.V.Sc. & A.H. is a 5½-year veterinary programme in the GADVASU admission rules. KCVAS combines veterinary study with clinical and animal-management teaching; professional-registration conditions should be checked with the relevant authorities.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for B.V.Sc. & A.H. at KCVAS?
faqs.answer: ₹1,80,000 / six months · 2026–27. KCVAS table 2.2.5(C), printedp 13: six-monthly tuition is ₹1,80,000 for University Quota, ₹3,80,000 forManagement Quota and ₹4,37,500 forSpecial Management Quota. Other six-monthly charges are ₹31,500. The published entry-time totals include one-time charges/security; hostel/mess and category terms must be read separately. Tuition applies to 4½ years of course work; KCVAS other charges continue during internship. No flat five-year total is inferred. Included charges: University-quota tuition only; other six-monthly charges, one-time fees, securities and accommodation are separate.

faqs.question: How does admission to KCVAS work?
faqs.answer: Use the university’s 2026–27 veterinary notices and the correct quota rules. A fourth-counselling notice names 30 October 2026; that is an event date, not evidence of an available KCVAS seat or a continuing application window. Confirm the current prospectus: Ask the admissions office for the applicable intake, subject requirements and selection rules before submitting an application. Request a written cost statement: Obtain tuition, compulsory charges, accommodation options and refund terms for the intended entry year.

faqs.question: What is the recorded ICAR scope for KCVAS?
faqs.answer: College of Khalsa College of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Amritsar: • B.V.Sc. & A.H. Programme (Intake- 60*), recorded term 2021-11-09 to 2026-11-08. This entry applies to the named unit and programme.

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at KCVAS?
faqs.answer: The clinical setting supports veterinary case-based teaching; request current rotation and internship arrangements.

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for KCVAS?
faqs.answer: The Veterinary Clinical Complex describes clinical medicine, surgery and radiology, and gynaecology/obstetrics services. It is located at Mahal, about two kilometres from the main campus according to the college. Accommodation availability, meal charges and transport arrangements for your entry year still need direct confirmation.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for KCVAS?
faqs.answer: The 2026–27 GADVASU prospectus states that KCVAS students eligible for the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme and admitted in the SC/ST university-quota category are charged the same fee as eligible GADVASU students. This is a restricted category rule, not a scholarship promise for management, NRI or every veterinary student. SC/ST Post-Matric Scholarship-linked fee treatment, University Quota: Prospectus section 2.2.5.2(iii) limits the rule to eligible SC/ST students under University Quota. Confirm current government eligibility, documents, reimbursement processing and the payable statement for your individual offer.

faqs.question: What training and outcome evidence is available for KCVAS?
faqs.answer: KCVAS describes training for employment and enterprise in the livestock sector. Clinical service and internship learning are educational components, not a measured placement outcome. A dated graduate-employment report and salary distribution were not verified.

faqs.question: Does KCVAS offer the agriculture degree covered on other profiles?
faqs.answer: The audited ICAR row explicitly lists B.V.Sc. & A.H. only. No B.Sc. Agriculture accreditation is inferred for KCVAS.

faqs.question: Which university is it affiliated to?
faqs.answer: The college and GADVASU identify affiliation to Guru Angad Dev Veterinary and Animal Sciences University, Ludhiana.

faqs.question: How long is the veterinary programme?
faqs.answer: GADVASU’s undergraduate rules specify 5½ years. This current programme statement is preferred to the college’s older five-year historical description.

sections.heading: Agriculture within a historic Amritsar college
paragraphs: Khalsa College was established in 1892 and is affiliated to Guru Nanak Dev University. Its agriculture department has a long academic history: the official department account records degree affiliation to Panjab University in 1931 and then GNDU in 1971, with postgraduate teaching developed in 1967.

The department describes dedicated agricultural teaching blocks and laboratories covering agronomy, crop protection, soil science, horticulture and agricultural economics. Its activity archive includes rural work experience, commercial beekeeping, mushroom cultivation and paddy-residue-management programmes. These dated examples help applicants understand the department’s practical orientation while leaving the current cohort’s exact activity calendar for direct confirmation.

sections.heading: Agriculture study at the Saikheda campus
paragraphs: G H Raisoni University’s agriculture course is located at Saikheda in Madhya Pradesh. The official programme page describes a four-year full-time honours degree divided into eight semesters. It brings together soil science, plant breeding, microbiology and crop-health subjects with practical exposure.

The university describes field practice, trips, study tours and projects within agricultural learning. Its course page also discusses work with farmers and agricultural companies as a way to connect classroom study with the sector. Applicants should ask for the current fieldwork calendar and internship arrangements, alongside a written fee statement and the admission rules for their intended entry year.

sections.heading: Agriculture study at Chaksu
paragraphs: Jagan Nath University, Jaipur was established in 2008 under Rajasthan legislation. Its Faculty of Agriculture dates the start of B.Sc. Agriculture teaching to 2014–15. The agriculture setting includes agronomic fields, teaching laboratories and farm machinery, linking the degree to crop-production practice.

The faculty describes protected cultivation, composting, irrigation and medicinal-plant units. These offer useful questions for a campus visit: how frequently students use each unit, which crops are grown for teaching, and how practical assessment works. The university offers other agriculture-related qualifications as well, but applicants should compare each programme’s admission requirements and accreditation separately.

paragraphs: Jaipur National University is a self-financed private institution sponsored by Mahima Shiksha Samiti. Its School of Agricultural Sciences presents agricultural study within the university’s wider range of programmes. Confirm the current prospectus: Ask the admissions office for the applicable intake, subject requirements and selection rules before submitting an application. sections.heading: Women’s agriculture education at Baru Sahib
paragraphs: Eternal University is based in the Baru Valley of Himachal Pradesh and is governed by The Kalgidhar Trust. Its registration portal explicitly restricts programmes to female applicants. This is a material admission condition for families considering agriculture at the university.

Dr. Khem Singh Gill Akal College of Agriculture was established within the university in 2014. The college’s published curriculum covers agronomy, horticulture, soils, crop improvement and protection, livestock production and food-related subjects. It also publishes laboratory manuals and a named academic roster. Applicants can assess how these subjects connect to their goals while confirming the current practical timetable, residential costs and entry-year eligibility directly.

sections.heading: Crop science within a wider agricultural faculty
paragraphs: The undergraduate agriculture course at AKS sits within a faculty that also publishes curricula for agricultural engineering, food technology and several postgraduate agricultural subjects. This allows applicants to distinguish a broad first degree from later specialist study rather than treating every agriculture-related course as the same qualification.

The agronomy department dates its establishment to 2014. Its published teaching and research interests include crop production, soil management and weed control. The department also describes farmer training and field demonstrations, giving a concrete extension context to academic work. Applicants can progress from the broad undergraduate degree to specialist agronomy study, subject to the published qualification and practical-work requirements.

faqs.question: Where is AKSU located?
faqs.answer: AKS University, Sherganj, Panna Road, Satna, Madhya Pradesh 485001

faqs.question: Which agriculture or allied programmes are covered at AKSU?
faqs.answer: This profile covers B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture; M.Sc. (Agriculture) Agronomy. The [courses and fees table](/university/aks-university/course-fee) separates the qualifications and published fee periods.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at AKSU?
faqs.answer: 2026-27: 12th PCM/PCB/Agriculture stream with at least 60%.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at AKSU?
faqs.answer: 4 years. The published curriculum introduces soil science, agronomy, horticulture, genetics, plant pathology and agricultural economics.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at AKSU?
faqs.answer: ₹55,000 / semester · 2026-27. Base fee. Published General/OBC university scholarship reduces this to INR 48,000; category conditions and additional charges need confirmation. Non-refundable registration INR 4,900. Included charges: Published tuition/course fee; additional charges must be checked separately.

faqs.question: How does admission to AKSU work?
faqs.answer: AKS links an online admission portal and publishes a 2026-27 fee-and-eligibility table. Applicants can compare the base semester fee with the university’s category-specific scholarship columns before requesting their final offer. Check the course requirements: Read the published agriculture qualification and any selection requirement under the university ordinance. Complete the application: AKS accepts its online form or an offline form obtained through the admissions office. Submit the required records: Provide qualifying records and identity/transfer/character documents from the official common checklist. Confirm admission and enrolment: After the admissions section issues confirmation, complete the specified payment, registration and enrolment formalities.

faqs.question: What is the recorded ICAR scope for AKSU?
faqs.answer: AKS University, Satna, M.P.: B. Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture (Intake- 240), recorded term 2022-10-11 to 2027-10-10. This entry applies to the named unit and programme.

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at AKSU?
faqs.answer: Department-led farmer training and demonstrations are described on the agronomy page. The B.Sc. curriculum assigns practical credit to subjects including soil science, crop physiology and entomology.

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for AKSU?
faqs.answer: The agronomy department reports practical training alongside classroom teaching. Its extension activities include workshops, field visits and demonstrations intended to connect university knowledge with farming practice. Accommodation availability, meal charges and transport arrangements for your entry year still need direct confirmation.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for AKSU?
faqs.answer: The 2026-27 table gives a General/OBC university scholarship of INR 7,000 per semester for B.Sc. Agriculture and INR 2,000 for M.Sc. Agronomy. Confirm award and continuation conditions before relying on the reduced payable fee. University scholarship: General/OBC fee table: Published semester reductions for the listed agriculture courses; individual eligibility is subject to university confirmation.

faqs.question: What training and outcome evidence is available for AKSU?
faqs.answer: The agronomy department describes campus recruitment, career counselling and preparation for interviews and CV writing. These are support activities; the checked page does not supply a dated agriculture placement rate or salary distribution.

faqs.question: Which AKS agriculture degree appears in the ICAR register?
faqs.answer: The audited entry names B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture for 11 October 2022 to 10 October 2027.

faqs.question: How long is the undergraduate agriculture course?
faqs.answer: The university admissions listing gives four years.

faqs.question: Does AKS offer postgraduate agronomy?
faqs.answer: Yes. Its agronomy department lists a two-year M.Sc. requiring a B.Sc. Agriculture qualification.

sections.heading: Agricultural study connected with campus food production
paragraphs: The Faculty of Agriculture offers more than one route into agricultural study. University sustainability reporting describes undergraduate agriculture, horticulture, agribusiness and food, nutrition and dietetics, together with postgraduate agricultural disciplines. Applicants should compare the science and business orientation of these qualifications before selecting a course.

The university reports that its farmland contributes produce to campus food services. A 2026 sustainability submission describes fruit, vegetable and cereal cultivation, together with apiculture and mushroom units. These activities place agricultural production within a working campus food system, while the different science and business degrees allow students to choose an emphasis suited to their interests.

institutions.summary: Rajasthan Vidyapeeth’s School of Agricultural Sciences operates at Dabok near Udaipur. Its course list spans undergraduate agriculture, specialist postgraduate study and agricultural research. The school’s stated priorities include crop management, postharvest value addition and knowledge transfer to farming communities in southern Rajasthan.

sections.heading: Agricultural education with a southern Rajasthan focus
paragraphs: The School of Agricultural Sciences is based at the university’s Dabok campus, rather than simply sharing the central administrative address in Udaipur. Its published teaching objectives address crop and pest management, preventing postharvest losses and taking agricultural knowledge to farming communities. These priorities provide useful context for applicants interested in extension as well as production science.

The official school page lists B.Sc. Agriculture, several M.Sc. Agriculture and Horticulture specialisations, an agribusiness MBA and doctoral study. These are distinct awards with different academic entry points. The published postgraduate list includes crop production, plant health, agricultural economics, extension and livestock management, together with fruit, vegetable and ornamental horticulture.

sections.heading: Field-based agricultural study in Coimbatore
paragraphs: Karunya dates its School of Agricultural Sciences to 2017. The current school page describes eleven academic divisions, covering crop, soil, plant-health, engineering and allied subjects. Its farm and laboratory setting supports a programme account that extends beyond lecture teaching to crop experiments, protected cultivation and agricultural enterprise learning.

Official sources list a four-year B.Sc. Agriculture together with postgraduate agronomy, genetics and plant breeding, and fruit science. Entry wording differs between the academics page and the brochure located during research, so applicants need the definitive course notice before selecting a school-subject or postgraduate route.

paragraphs: Find the complete set on [Karunya Institute of Technology and Sciences FAQs](/university/karunya-institute-of-technology-and-sciences/faqs).

faqs.question: Where is KITS located?
faqs.answer: Karunya Institute of Technology and Sciences, Karunya Nagar, Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu 641114

faqs.question: Which agriculture or allied programmes are covered at KITS?
faqs.answer: This profile covers B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture; M.Sc. (Agriculture) Agronomy; M.Sc. (Agriculture) Genetics and Plant Breeding; M.Sc. (Horticulture) Fruit Sciences. The [courses and fees table](/university/karunya-institute-of-technology-and-sciences/course-fee) separates the qualifications and published fee periods.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at KITS?
faqs.answer: The 2027 UG admissions page states a minimum 60% qualifying-examination requirement for confirmation. Confirm the programme-specific subjects for that intake; older academic pages and brochures list different combinations and thresholds.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at KITS?
faqs.answer: 4 years. The school describes crop, soil and plant-health study linked with field practice.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at KITS?
faqs.answer: ₹1,46,750 / semester · 2026-27. Tuition for each of eight semesters in the 2026-30 cohort fee sheet; one-time admission fee INR 10,000; examination fees extra. Included charges: Published tuition/course fee; additional charges must be checked separately.

faqs.question: How does admission to KITS work?
faqs.answer: The live official UG admissions page now describes the 2027 cycle. It states that KEE 2027 is mandatory for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture and that confirmation depends on the stated qualifying-examination requirements. Treat these as next-cycle instructions; the 2026–30 cohort fee sheet below remains explicitly labelled by its own source session. Older academic and brochure descriptions differ, so request the exact intake-year subject rules. Confirm the course: Use the official programme contact to confirm that the listed degree is taking applications for your intended intake. Request the intake notice: Ask for the applicable selection rules, fee breakdown and document checklist before submitting an application.

faqs.question: What is the recorded ICAR scope for KITS?
faqs.answer: Karunya Institute of Technology and Sciences (Deemed University), Coimbatore: B. Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture (Intake-180), recorded term 2022-10-11 to 2027-10-10. This entry applies to the named unit and programme.

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at KITS?
faqs.answer: The school describes instructional and research farmland, polyhouses, mist chambers and research plots. Its brochure additionally identifies experiential-learning modules, an agrometeorological observatory and an automatic weather station.

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for KITS?
faqs.answer: The school describes instructional and research farmland, polyhouses, mist chambers and research plots. Its brochure additionally identifies experiential-learning modules, an agrometeorological observatory and an automatic weather station. Accommodation availability, meal charges and transport arrangements for your entry year still need direct confirmation.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for KITS?
faqs.answer: Karunya’s 2026–27 scholarship page explicitly includes B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture in its Indian-student merit grid. The separate Founder’s Scholarship offers a limited 100% tuition waiver for eligible Indian Christian applicants; its 2026 application and selection dates have passed. B.Sc. Agriculture Indian-student merit grid, 2026–27: The agriculture column lists INR 1,20,000 at 95% PCM/PCB, INR 60,000 at 90%, and INR 40,000 at 85%. These are scholarship amounts, not net tuition payable. Obtain the approved award and applicable continuation terms. Founder’s Scholarship 2026–27: Limited 100% tuition waiver for selected Indian Christian applicants with at least 90% PCM/PCB and annual family income below INR 8 lakh. Screening includes documentary verification and interview. The 29 May 2026 deadline is past.

faqs.question: What training and outcome evidence is available for KITS?
faqs.answer: Karunya Institute of Technology and Sciences publishes an Agriculture and Allied Sectors submission for NIRF 2026. Its programme-duration cohorts report the graduating group, students placed, students entering higher studies and the median salary of placed graduates. These historical institutional submissions are not a placement promise or a salary estimate for every student or individual specialisation.

faqs.question: When did Karunya’s agriculture school begin?
faqs.answer: The school’s official page states 2017; that is the school date, not the university’s founding year.

faqs.question: Which agricultural programmes are listed?
faqs.answer: The current school page names B.Sc. Agriculture and master’s courses in agronomy, genetics and plant breeding, and fruit sciences.

faqs.question: Are protected-cultivation facilities documented?
faqs.answer: Yes. The school names polyhouses and mist chambers alongside research plots.

sections.heading: Agriculture courses spanning crops, horticulture and engineering
paragraphs: SGVU was established through Rajasthan legislation in 2008. Its agriculture landing page lists B.Sc. Agriculture, agricultural engineering and master’s and doctoral subjects in agriculture and horticulture. The undergraduate agriculture degree is the programme explicitly printed in the checked ICAR row.

The school’s current facilities description includes soil science, plant pathology, entomology and biotechnology laboratories. Hydroponics and protected cultivation add a horticultural component to field-based crop study. The programme catalogue includes both agricultural science and engineering, while the master’s subject list extends from crop production and protection to horticultural specialisations.

sections.heading: Agricultural study across production and plant-health disciplines
paragraphs: SGRRU places agriculture in a dedicated constituent school. Its departmental list includes agronomy, horticulture, seed science, soil science, entomology, plant pathology, genetics and plant breeding, and food technology. For an undergraduate applicant, this shows the range of scientific subjects surrounding the agriculture degree rather than a single crop specialism.

The B.Sc. course page describes an eight-semester programme with laboratory and farm learning. Its eligibility text accepts specified science, agriculture or horticulture backgrounds. A 2025 prospectus names an entrance examination, whereas the current webpage only says admission follows university norms. Applicants should request the rule for their intended intake rather than assuming that an older route is unchanged.

sections.heading: A Vellore agriculture school with clear 2026 entry rules
paragraphs: VAIAL is VIT’s School of Agricultural Innovations and Advanced Learning. Its published activities combine degree teaching, agricultural research and farmer outreach. The school describes facilities for crop and horticultural work, analytical teaching laboratories, botanical and medicinal gardens, composting and farm machinery. Its events record includes training on organic farming, coconut cultivation and vegetable value addition.

The 2026-27 agriculture portal provides unusually specific applicant information: selection uses qualifying-examination merit, followed by online counselling. It states academic, residency and age conditions, and publishes three tuition categories. These are Vellore agriculture rules; applicants should not assume the same process applies to other VIT campuses or engineering programmes.

sections.heading: Agriculture teaching with a rural development context
paragraphs: RNTU’s agriculture faculty describes its original purpose as expanding agricultural education in underserved parts of Raisen district. The degree began in 2015-16. The current course account covers agronomy, horticulture, soil science, plant health, breeding, economics and extension, bringing production science and the social setting of farming into the same undergraduate route.

The published programme structure includes village surveys, soil sampling, plant-protection interventions and agro-industrial attachment. It also lists enterprise learning options such as beekeeping, mushroom cultivation and seed production. These are curriculum descriptions; applicants should ask which modules will actually run for their cohort and how the practical timetable is organised.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at GIET University?
faqs.answer: Historical 2020 official notice: 10+2 PCM/PCB, 50% general and 45% SC/ST; current intake criteria require confirmation.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at GIET University?
faqs.answer: 4 years (8 semesters). A full-time agricultural science degree with crop-production plots and Student READY activities.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at GIET University?
faqs.answer: ₹1,60,000 / year · 2024-25. Historical B.Sc. Agriculture annual fee, also shown as INR80,000 per semester. Other charges separate; current applicability not established. Included charges: Published programme fee; other charges are separate unless stated.

faqs.question: How does admission to GIET University work?
faqs.answer: The official entrance page identifies GIETEE for B.Sc. Agriculture and displays 2026-27 material, alongside a newer 2027 banner and an old 2020 fee note. Applicants need the specific intake prospectus rather than relying on mixed-year page labels. Confirm the course: Use the official programme contact to confirm that the listed degree is taking applications for your intended intake. Request the intake notice: Ask for the applicable selection rules, fee breakdown and document checklist before submitting an application.

faqs.question: What is the recorded ICAR scope for GIET University?

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at GIET University?
faqs.answer: A dated August 2026 university report records a farmer exposure visit to Instructional Farm-I and research demonstration plots.

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for GIET University?
faqs.answer: Agriculture hostel allocation: The school states that five hostels serve agriculture students: three for boys and two for girls. Its description gives three to four students per room; individual allocations require confirmation. Dining and drinking water: The school describes a central mess, monitored food provision and hostel water coolers. Hostel recreation and emergency support: The facility account lists indoor games, gymnasiums and emergency ambulance provision, alongside internet access.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for GIET University?
faqs.answer: GIET’s general scholarship page contains schemes with different programme scopes, including GIETEE/Board-of-Governance categories explicitly marked B.Tech-only. Agriculture applicants should ask which government reimbursement or institutional assistance actually applies to their course and entry year. Engineering award limits should not be transferred to agriculture.

faqs.question: What training and outcome evidence is available for GIET University?
faqs.answer: GIET University publishes an Agriculture and Allied Sectors submission for NIRF 2026. Its programme-duration cohorts report the graduating group, students placed, students entering higher studies and the median salary of placed graduates. These historical institutional submissions are not a placement promise or a salary estimate for every student or individual specialisation.

faqs.question: When was GIET’s agriculture school established?
faqs.answer: The official school account states 2017.

faqs.question: Is agricultural admission through GIETEE?
faqs.answer: The entrance page explicitly includes B.Sc. Agriculture among GIETEE programmes; the current intake rules still need confirmation.

faqs.question: Are students assigned crop plots?
faqs.answer: The instructional-farm page says separate plots are allotted to undergraduate students for crop-production activities.

Its official homepage identifies affiliation to Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture and Technology, Udaipur. The course page lists B.Sc. (Hons.) sections.heading: Agriculture learning in Sri Ganganagar
paragraphs: Tantia’s agriculture faculty introduced its four-year B.Sc. Agriculture programme in the 2015-16 academic session. The official programme catalogue also lists two-year agricultural master’s study across crop, soil, horticultural, economic and extension subjects. These subject choices provide a useful distinction between a broad undergraduate course and later agricultural specialisation.

The faculty’s infrastructure page describes an irrigated agriculture farm for technical training, together with laboratories and library facilities. The university’s revised 2025-26 brochure gives separate B.Sc. fee rows for JET and CUET. The fee distinction is historical evidence for that session and should not be carried into another admission year without a fresh schedule.

institutions.summary: At Sarisa in West Bengal, The Neotia University brings crop science, laboratory work and rural learning together through its School of Agriculture and Allied Sciences. Its four-year agriculture degree includes village attachment and agro-industrial experience, with teaching extending across soils, crops, plant protection, horticulture and farm economics.

sections.heading: Agriculture study near Diamond Harbour
paragraphs: TNU’s agriculture course connects crop science with work in farming environments. Its published curriculum includes soil science, horticulture, plant protection, genetics and agricultural economics. The degree page describes four years of study, with rural agricultural experience and an agro-industrial attachment in the final stage.

The school’s older official brochure describes teaching farms, laboratories and small production units, including mushroom and apiculture activity. Such settings connect scientific observation with day-to-day production decisions. The 2026–27 fee schedule identifies the agriculture bachelor’s degree alongside agribusiness, diploma and postgraduate routes, giving applicants distinct study options to compare.

institutions.summary: Centurion’s Odisha agriculture and fisheries schools connect degree study with working fields, production enterprises and aquaculture facilities. At Paralakhemundi, agricultural learning includes rural and industrial attachments, while fisheries students study aquatic production, health, processing and resource management in a separate specialist school.

sections.heading: Two allied schools within one Odisha university
paragraphs: The M.S. Swaminathan School of Agriculture describes learning through fields, laboratories and enterprise activity. Its school page identifies agronomy, crop improvement, horticulture, soil science and extension as teaching and research areas. Student READY activities connect experiential work, rural exposure and agro-industrial attachment.

The School of Fisheries provides another applied pathway at Paralakhemundi. Its regulations describe aquaculture, fish processing, aquatic health and resource management, supported by training ponds, a hatchery and specialist production activity. Agriculture and fisheries therefore offer different practical settings within the university, and applicants can compare crop-based, engineering, agribusiness and aquatic-science routes according to their interests.

faqs.question: Where is CUTM located?
faqs.answer: Village Alluri Nagar, P.O. R Sitapur, via Uppalada, Paralakhemundi, Gajapati, Odisha 761211

faqs.question: Which agriculture or allied programmes are covered at CUTM?
faqs.answer: This profile covers B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture; B.Tech. Agricultural Engineering; M.Sc. (Agri.) Agronomy; M.Sc. (Agri.) Agricultural Extension Education; M.Sc. (Agri.) Genetics and Plant Breeding; M.Sc. (Hort.) Vegetable Science; MBA Agribusiness Management; Bachelor of Fisheries Science (B.F.Sc.). The [courses and fees table](/university/centurion-university-of-technology-and-management/course-fee) separates the qualifications and published fee periods.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at CUTM?
faqs.answer: The official programme page specifies 50% in 10+2 Science and prints the subject combination as Physics/Math, Chemistry, Biology. Confirm that wording against the intake-year bulletin.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at CUTM?
faqs.answer: 4 years. Crop, resource and rural-learning undergraduate route.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at CUTM?
faqs.answer: ₹1,50,000 / year · 2026. Separate first-year B.Sc./M.Sc. Agriculture charges total ₹30,000; confirm cohort applicability. Included charges: Paralakhemundi published programme fee.

faqs.question: How does admission to CUTM work?
faqs.answer: Choose the agriculture, agricultural-engineering, fisheries or agribusiness route before checking entry rules. The fee table labels its Paralakhemundi rows 2026 but retains a 2025–26 heading; obtain a cohort-specific statement including other fees and accommodation. Choose the school and course: Confirm agriculture, engineering, agribusiness or fisheries and its teaching campus before applying. Check the current entry rules: Use the linked admissions portal to obtain the relevant intake-year eligibility and fee notice.

faqs.question: What is the recorded ICAR scope for CUTM?
faqs.answer: M.S. Swaminathan School of Agriculture: • B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture (intake 240) • B.Tech. Agricultural Engineering (intake 30); • MSc. (Agri) Agronomy (inatke20) • M.Sc. (Agri) Agricultural Extension Education (intake 10) • M.Sc. (Agri.) Genetics and Plant Breeding (intake 10) • M.Sc. (Hort.) Vegetable Science (intake 10) • MBA Agribusiness Management (intake 10), recorded term 2024-03-29 to 2029-03-28. School of Fisheries: B. F. Sc. (Intake- 40), recorded term 2024-02-08 to 2029-02-07. This entry applies to the named unit and programme.

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at CUTM?
faqs.answer: Agriculture READY activities include experiential learning, rural work and agro-industrial attachment. Fisheries regulations describe hands-on aquaponics and ornamental fish culture.

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for CUTM?
faqs.answer: Agriculture uses research farms and laboratories, while fisheries has its own aquaculture teaching resources documented in the 2022 regulations. Accommodation availability, meal charges and transport arrangements for your entry year still need direct confirmation.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for CUTM?
faqs.answer: The published Amrit Kaal table includes Agricultural Engineering within its non-CSE B.Tech group at Paralakhemundi/Bhubaneswar. It sets first-year fee concessions by qualifying results. This is not evidence of the same award for B.Sc. Agriculture, M.Sc. Agriculture or Fisheries, and the page does not give a governing academic year. Amrit Kaal scholarship: non-CSE B.Tech including Agri: The official table lists 10% for 60–70% qualifying marks and 15% for 70–80%; a separate top-score/JEE/OJEE band lists 20%. These are first-year fee concessions. Boundary wording, programme/campus eligibility and the current policy must be confirmed in the award letter.

faqs.question: What training and outcome evidence is available for CUTM?
faqs.answer: The university's NIRF 2026 Agriculture and Allied Sectors submission reports graduates, placements, higher-study progression and the median annual salary of placed graduates for the cohorts below. The figures apply to the reported programme-duration group, rather than an individual specialisation, and do not predict an applicant's future outcome.

faqs.question: Why are two ICAR units shown for Centurion?
faqs.answer: Agriculture and fisheries have separate source rows; they belong to one Odisha university profile.

faqs.question: Does the fisheries degree use the agriculture accreditation dates?
faqs.answer: No. The fisheries record runs from 8 February 2024 to 7 February 2029.

faqs.question: Where is the fisheries school described in the regulations?
faqs.answer: The July 2022 regulations place it at the Paralakhemundi campus in Gajapati district.

sections.heading: Agriculture foundations and specialist postgraduate study
paragraphs: LPU’s agriculture school brings crop, livestock and post-harvest learning into one academic setting. Its facilities page identifies an animal husbandry and dairy unit, agricultural farms and subject laboratories. The breadth matters when comparing a general agriculture degree with a focused postgraduate specialisation.

The bachelor’s degree offers a broad entry to agriculture, while the school’s master’s subjects allow a closer focus on agronomy, genetics, plant protection, soils or horticulture. These choices share an agricultural setting but serve different stages of study. The official CUET 2026 mapping supplies a dated bachelor’s eligibility reference, and the admissions office can clarify how that route fits the intended intake.

sections.heading: Agriculture teaching in the Krishnankoil setting
paragraphs: KARE’s published agriculture curriculum links crop production and improvement with natural resources, agricultural economics and extension. The 2022 syllabus provides a detailed academic reference for prospective students who want to examine course content beyond a programme title.

The Kalasalingam Anandammal Farm gives the school a practical setting for crop work. KARE’s institutional history begins with an engineering college in 1984 and records university status from 2006.

sections.heading: An affiliated agriculture college at Etcherla
paragraphs: ANGRAU distinguishes SKYCAS from its constituent government colleges by listing it among affiliated agriculture colleges. The directory places it at Etcherla and gives 2016 as its establishment year. The college therefore needs to be assessed as an affiliated institution with its own teaching setting, while the university provides the academic and admission framework described in official notices.

For the 2026–27 session, the college is included in ANGRAU’s brochure for participating affiliated institutions. Category A admission uses AP EAPCET 2026 ranks, making the university’s counselling instructions central to the application process. Students comparing an affiliated college with an ANGRAU constituent college should check the named institution and admission category carefully, because the college identity and the university’s academic framework play different roles.

sections.heading: Agriculture study and field learning at Mathura
paragraphs: GLA’s faculty page presents agriculture teaching around crop science, research and extension. It identifies field experiments, internships and industry exposure within its approach to experiential learning. The faculty also describes emerging areas such as precision agriculture and value addition, giving applicants a clearer picture than a general university overview alone.

The undergraduate page gives practical examples including vegetables, herbs and flowers, making the faculty’s crop-based work more tangible. Its entry criteria can be read alongside the 2026–27 Mathura fee schedule, which sets out academic charges for each of the four years. The faculty also describes postgraduate and doctoral teaching, allowing applicants to distinguish a broad first degree from later specialist study.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at Shri Shivaji Agriculture College?
faqs.answer: 2026–27 state prospectus: Class 12 Science with PCB/PCMB/PCM or Intermediate Agriculture and English passed; minimum 45% aggregate for Open applicants and 40% for the specified reserved categories. The prospectus requires an applicable entrance score above zero; follow its programme/category and candidature rules.

faqs.answer: 4 years (8 semesters); study format: Full time. An undergraduate agriculture programme taught within the PDKV-affiliated college setting.

faqs.question: How does admission to Shri Shivaji Agriculture College work?
faqs.answer: The 2026–27 state prospectus identifies Shri Shivaji as an aided PDKV-affiliated agriculture college, institution code 11107, with an intake of 120. Admission follows the state agriculture CAP framework. Its published final admission cutoff was 17 September 2026; this historical calendar does not establish an open vacancy. Check the official state framework: Use the 2026–27 agriculture prospectus and college code 11107 to verify candidature, entrance and reservation rules. Use the relevant CAP round: Follow registration, preference submission, allotment and reporting instructions. The published 2026–27 admission cutoff was 17 September 2026, so ask the authority about any separate later notice. Verify reporting and cost: Confirm the full document list and approved aided-college fee statement before reporting or paying.

sections.heading: Agriculture learning through departments, villages and research
paragraphs: SOA’s Institute of Agricultural Sciences lists departments spanning agricultural engineering, economics, extension, crop production, plant protection and horticulture. The 2026 programme list describes a four-year agriculture bachelor’s degree and two-year master’s routes, providing both a broad foundation and routes into specialised study.

A 2026 university report describes village attachment in Khordha district, where students assessed cropping systems and worked on village action plans. Another 2026 report records an ICAR-CRRI partnership concerning rice research and postgraduate training. These are documented examples of academic activity; access to a particular research placement still depends on the programme and arrangements in force.

faqs.question: Where is AUS located?
faqs.answer: NH-52, Namsai, Arunachal Pradesh 792103

faqs.question: Which agriculture or allied programmes are covered at AUS?
faqs.answer: This profile covers B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture. The [courses and fees table](/university/arunachal-university-of-studies/course-fee) separates the qualifications and published fee periods.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at AUS?
faqs.answer: 2026–27 prospectus: first-year entry requires 10+2 in Science/Agriculture or equivalent; second-year entry requires a Diploma in Agriculture or equivalent. The agriculture row does not specify minimum marks or the selection test.

faqs.question: How long is B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at AUS?
faqs.answer: 4 years (8 semesters). The 2026–27 prospectus lists an eight-semester agriculture honours degree, with separate first-year and second-year entry qualifications.

faqs.question: What fee is documented for B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture at AUS?
faqs.answer: ₹90,000 / year · 2026-2027. Published annual amount for the agriculture bachelor’s degree. Obtain a complete payable statement; adjacent Life Sciences examination/OJT charges do not establish agriculture charges. Included charges: Annual programme fee in the 2026–27 agriculture table; itemised compulsory, residential and other charges are not specified in this row.

faqs.question: How does admission to AUS work?
faqs.answer: The official 2026–27 prospectus establishes agriculture duration, entry qualifications and an annual fee. It does not settle minimum marks or selection-test rules in the agriculture row. The homepage identifies an application portal, which returned 403 when independently opened; confirm the operative selection notice before paying. Select the correct entry year: Use the 2026–27 prospectus to distinguish first-year entry from diploma-based second-year entry. Confirm selection and complete charges: Request the current entrance/merit instructions and an itemised fee statement from the published university contacts.

faqs.question: What is the recorded ICAR scope for AUS?
faqs.answer: Arunachal University of Studies: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture (Intake- 120), recorded term 2025-09-30 to 2030-09-29. This entry applies to the named unit and programme.

faqs.question: What practical learning is described at AUS?
faqs.answer: Fourth-year AUS agriculture students visited KVK demonstrations of climate-resilient technologies in August 2025.

faqs.question: What student facilities are documented for AUS?
faqs.answer: ICAR’s 21 August 2025 report describes an agriculture student visit to KVK Namsai at Momong. It supports external practical exposure rather than a claim about ownership of the KVK facilities. Accommodation availability, meal charges and transport arrangements for your entry year still need direct confirmation.

faqs.question: What scholarship information is available for AUS?
faqs.answer: The 2026–27 agriculture table describes government fee-reimbursement assistance for eligible APST students, subject to scheme terms and approval. The university also limits concurrent scholarship applications to one award. Its separate scholarship form deadline of 30 October 2026 is already past. Conditional APST fee-reimbursement assistance: The 2026–27 agriculture table states reimbursement up to ₹50,000 for APST candidates with annual family income below ₹2,50,000, under Central/State government schemes and prescribed terms. This is a maximum conditional benefit, not an automatic deduction or a guaranteed award; the brochure does not give renewal rules. Government stipend / scholarship application route: The university directs eligible students to Arunachal Pradesh or Government of India granting agencies and limits concurrent applications to one award. The listed university submission deadline was30October2026; no current agriculture-specific entitlement is established.

faqs.question: What training and outcome evidence is available for AUS?
faqs.answer: A dated agriculture placement report and current institutional career-support details were not verified from accessible official material.

faqs.question: Is AUS privately funded?
faqs.answer: WHED identifies its funding as private, and the district directory labels it a private university.

faqs.question: Which agriculture course appears in the 2025 entrance mapping?
faqs.answer: Bachelor of Science (Honours–Agriculture).

faqs.question: What practical exposure has been independently documented?
faqs.answer: ICAR reported an August 2025 visit by fourth-year agriculture students to KVK Namsai at Momong.

sections.heading: From agricultural foundations to agronomy specialisation
paragraphs: ITM’s agriculture bachelor’s curriculum is organised around fundamental sciences, production systems and later skill development. The university’s brochure places the school at its Sithouli setting and identifies an instructional farm, laboratory and library resources. A separate agronomy master’s course provides a focused postgraduate route.

The programme pages identify agriculture partnerships with research institutions and describe Student READY learning. For career comparisons, ITM also publishes an agriculture-and-allied-sector NIRF submission with dated undergraduate and postgraduate outcomes. These grouped returns are more specific than the university’s overall salary counters, though they still should not be read as a guarantee for one degree or a future student.

sections.heading: Agriculture study with rural and enterprise exposure
paragraphs: RNBGU’s agriculture school describes a curriculum that connects classroom subjects with farms and commercial activity. Its published pedagogy includes rural agricultural work experience, skill and entrepreneurship modules, and demonstrations involving crop production, nurseries and horticultural crops. The programme page lists a four-year bachelor’s degree.

The university was established under a Rajasthan act in 2015. Its agriculture course pages distinguish Rajasthan-domicile applicants from those outside the state. Applicants should therefore compare the correct category, tuition, examination fee and one-time enrolment charges. The university also publishes a dated 2026 scholarship policy, which specifies that awards apply to tuition and have academic continuation conditions.

sections.heading: Agriculture departments within a historic Jaunpur college
paragraphs: T.D. College traces its origins to a school founded by Sri Tilak Dhari Singh in 1914; its own history dates degree-college status to July 1947. Located in Husainabad, Jaunpur, it is a privately managed grant-in-aid college affiliated to Veer Bahadur Singh Purvanchal University. The founding year therefore describes the institution’s origins rather than the start of degree-level agriculture.

The agriculture faculty spans agronomy, genetics and plant breeding, agricultural economics, engineering, entomology, extension, horticulture, plant pathology, animal husbandry and soil science. The undergraduate agriculture degree is complemented by six postgraduate specialisms in the ICAR register. Applicants interested in a particular specialism can compare the departmental faculty list and the current entrance bulletin before choosing a route.

sections.heading: Agricultural education at Apex University, Jaipur (School of Agricultural Sciences)
paragraphs: Apex University, Jaipur operates its dedicated School of Agricultural Sciences at Jaipur, Rajasthan, offering B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture, M.Sc. Agriculture (Agronomy), MBA Agribusiness Management. The curriculum follows the 5th Deans’ Committee / ICAR credit structure with core courses in agronomy, genetics and plant breeding, soil science, entomology, plant pathology, horticulture, agricultural economics and extension education.

Applicants can enter the four-year B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture programme through Rajasthan JET / CUET (UG) / Apex Common Entrance Test (ACET). Instructional crop farm at the Achrol campus along NH-48 with polyhouse horticulture plots, soil-water testing laboratory and RAWE rural attachment in Jaipur district villages. Candidates comparing private agriculture universities in Rajasthan should verify both state JET counselling seat matrices and cohort-specific statutory accreditation terms before locking their choice.
